learn.hook: What is smaller than 1 but bigger than 0? A whole secret world of numbers lives behind the decimal point!
points: Cut one whole into 10 equal parts. Each part is one tenth, written 1/10 or 0.1.
Cut one whole into 100 equal parts. Each part is one hundredth, written 1/100 or 0.01.
The decimal point separates the whole part (on the left) from the parts smaller than one (on the right).
2.7 means 2 wholes and 7 tenths, that is 2 + 7/10.
10 tenths make 1 whole, and 10 hundredths make 1 tenth.

steps: The whole part is 3, so write 3 before the point
4 tenths go in the first place after the point
6 hundredths go in the second place after the point

learn.reallife: A fever of 100.2 °F, a long jump of 3.45 m and prices like ₹49.50 all use decimals.

quiz.q: Which decimal shows 7/10?
quiz.explain: 7/10 means 7 tenths. The first place after the point is tenths, so it is 0.7.
quiz.mistake: Puts the 7 in the hundredths place

quiz.q: Meena ate 3 of the 10 equal pieces of a chocolate bar. What decimal part of the bar did she eat?
quiz.explain: 3 pieces out of 10 equal pieces is 3/10 = 0.3.
quiz.mistake: Writes the part she did not eat, or puts 3 in the hundredths place

quiz.q: Write 2 + 5/10 + 8/100 as a decimal.
quiz.explain: 2 is the whole part, 5 goes in the tenths place and 8 in the hundredths place: 2.58.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the tenths and hundredths places

quiz.q: How many hundredths are there in 0.4?
quiz.explain: 1 tenth = 10 hundredths, so 4 tenths = 40 hundredths. Indeed 0.4 = 0.40.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 4 tenths is the same as 4 hundredths

quiz.q: Which fraction is the same as 0.09?
quiz.explain: 0.09 has 9 in the hundredths place, so it is 9 hundredths = 9/100.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one digit after the point always means tenths

quiz.q: What is 15 tenths written as a decimal?
quiz.explain: 10 tenths make 1 whole. 15 tenths = 10 tenths + 5 tenths = 1.5.
quiz.mistake: Writes the 15 straight after the point

quiz.q: Arjun's school is 1 km and 3 tenths of a km from his home. Which decimal shows this?
quiz.explain: 1 whole km and 3 tenths is 1 + 0.3 = 1.3 km.
quiz.mistake: Puts the 3 in the hundredths place

quiz.q: What does 0.25 mean?
quiz.explain: In 0.25 the 2 is in the tenths place and the 5 is in the hundredths place.
quiz.mistake: Reads the digits after the point in the wrong places

teach.ask: Gappu sees 0.3 written on a juice bottle label. What does 0.3 mean? Explain it to him!
teach.praise: Chirp chirp! 3 out of 10 equal parts — Gappu understands now!
teach.nudge: Into how many equal parts do we cut the whole for tenths?

learn.hook: Is 0.5 smaller than 0.45 because it has fewer digits? Nope! Let's find out why.
points: After the decimal point the places are tenths, hundredths, thousandths, and so on.
Each place is 10 times smaller than the place to its left.
In 3.04 the 4 is in the hundredths place, so its value is 0.04.
To compare decimals, first compare the whole parts, then tenths, then hundredths.
Zeros at the end after the point do not change the value: 0.5 = 0.50 = 0.500.

steps: Compare tenths: 4.07 has 0 tenths, 4.7 has 7 tenths

learn.reallife: When comparing the prices ₹45.50 and ₹45.05, or race times like 12.4 s and 12.35 s, you compare decimals.

games.title: Decimal detective
items: A zero at the end after the point does not change the value.
0.25 has 2 tenths and 0.3 has 3 tenths, so 0.3 is greater.
In 6.738 the digit 3 is in the hundredths place.
7 is tenths, 3 is hundredths and 8 is thousandths.
A decimal with more digits is always the bigger number.
0.123 has more digits but is smaller than 0.5.
The whole part 2 is less than 3, so 2.9 is smaller.

quiz.q: What is the place value of 6 in 25.36?
quiz.explain: 6 is the second digit after the point, which is the hundredths place. Its value is 6 hundredths = 0.06.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the first place after the point is hundredths

quiz.q: Which is greater: 0.8 or 0.75?
quiz.explain: Compare tenths: 0.8 has 8 tenths and 0.75 has 7 tenths. So 0.8 is greater. (0.8 = 0.80 and 80 > 75.)
quiz.mistake: Thinks 75 is bigger than 8, so 0.75 must be bigger

quiz.q: Which list goes from smallest to largest?
quiz.explain: Write them as hundredths: 0.29, 0.30 and 0.31. Now it is easy to see 29 < 30 < 31.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the number with fewer digits is the smallest

quiz.q: A number line from 2 to 3 is cut into 10 equal parts. A dot sits on the 4th mark after 2. What number is it?
quiz.explain: Each small part is one tenth. 4 tenths after 2 is 2.4.
quiz.mistake: Thinks each small part is a hundredth

quiz.q: Riya's long jump was 3.45 m and Kabir's was 3.5 m. How much farther did Kabir jump?
quiz.explain: Write 3.5 as 3.50. Then 3.50 − 3.45 = 0.05 m. Kabir jumped 5 cm farther.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 3.45 is longer because 45 is more than 5

quiz.q: In 47.293, which digit is in the hundredths place?
quiz.explain: After the point: 2 is tenths, 9 is hundredths and 3 is thousandths.
quiz.mistake: Counts places from the left of the whole number

quiz.q: Which number is equal to 5.3?
quiz.explain: Adding a zero at the end after the point does not change the value, so 5.3 = 5.30.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any zero changes the value, even at the end

quiz.explain: 1 one, 2 tenths, 5 hundredths and 3 thousandths make 1.253.
quiz.mistake: Puts the digits in the wrong places

teach.ask: Gappu thinks 0.35 is bigger than 0.4 because 35 is bigger than 4. Help him compare them correctly!
teach.praise: Tweet! 4 tenths beats 3 tenths — Gappu will never be fooled again!
teach.nudge: Which place after the point should we compare first?

learn.hook: Your height might be 1.45 m — that tiny dot lets a single number hold metres AND centimetres!
points: 1 kg = 1000 g, so 1 g = 0.001 kg. Also 1 km = 1000 m.
To add or subtract decimals, line up the decimal points, fill empty places with zeros, then work as usual.

example.q: Aisha buys 1 kg 250 g of rice and 750 g of dal. What is the total weight in kg?

learn.reallife: Tailors measure cloth in metres like 2.25 m, shops weigh vegetables as 1.5 kg, and bills show rupees and paise like ₹36.75.

quiz.q: A pencil is 8 cm 4 mm long. What is its length in cm?
quiz.explain: 10 mm = 1 cm, so 4 mm = 0.4 cm. The pencil is 8 + 0.4 = 8.4 cm.
quiz.mistake: Thinks there are 100 mm in a cm

quiz.q: Write 65 cm in metres.
quiz.mistake: Divides by 10 instead of 100

quiz.q: A bag of atta weighs 2.5 kg. How many grams is that?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by 100 instead of 1000

quiz.q: Kabir has ₹12.50. He spends ₹4.75 on juice. How much money is left?
quiz.explain: Line up the points: 12.50 − 4.75 = 7.75.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the smaller paise digit from the bigger one instead of borrowing

quiz.q: Meena walked 1.25 km to the market and then 0.8 km to her aunt's house. How far did she walk in all?
quiz.explain: Line up the points: 1.25 + 0.80 = 2.05 km.
quiz.mistake: Lines up the last digits instead of the decimal points (1.25 + 0.08)

quiz.q: Which is longer: 1.5 m or 145 cm?
quiz.explain: 1.5 m = 150 cm, and 150 cm is more than 145 cm.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 145 is bigger than 1.5 without changing the units

quiz.q: Write 3 kg 40 g in kg.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 40 g is 0.4 kg

quiz.q: Riya has a 5 m ribbon. She cuts off 1.75 m for a rangoli border. How much ribbon is left?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to write 5 as 5.00 and slips while borrowing

teach.ask: Gappu wants to add 2.5 kg and 1.25 kg of mangoes. How should he add decimals?
teach.praise: Hooray! 3.75 kg of mangoes — Gappu is ready for a mango party!
teach.nudge: What must be in line when we write the numbers one below the other?
